education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the

BUREAU     OF   INDIAN    STANDARDS 

MANAK    BHAVAN,   9    BAHADUR    SHAH    ZAFAR     MARG 
NEW  DELHI  110002 

July  1990  Price  Groap  4 


Power  Gables  Sectional  Committee,  ETD  9 


F()  REWORD 

This  Indian  Standard  (First  Revision)  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  on 
23  January  1990,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the  Power  Cables  Sectional  Committee  had  been 
approved  by  the  Eiecfrotechnical  Division  Council. 

The  requirements  of  welding  cables  were  earlier  covered  in  IS  434  (  Parts  1  and  2)  :  1964  and 
IS  434  (Part  2):  19^4  'Rubber  insulated  cables;  Part  1  With  copper  conductors  (rewed), 
Part  2  With  aluminium  conductors  (revised}*  at  the  time  of  revision  of  these  standards,  a  need 
was  felt  to  have  a  separate  standard  for  welding  cables.  This  separate  standard  (IS  9857) 
was  published  in  1981.  This  revision  is  brought  out  to  align  it  with  IS  8130  :  1984  'Conductors 
for  insulated  electric  cables  and  flexible  cords  (first  revision  )\  IS  6380  :  1984  'Elastomeric 
insulation  and  sheath  of  electric  cables  (  first  revision  Y ,  and  IS  10810  :  1984  'Methods  of  test  for 
cables'. 

In  this  standaid,  the  requirement  for  cables  with  copper  as  well  as  aluminium  conductors  have 
been  specified.  The  limitations  of  aluminium  as  a  conductor  for  welding  cables  have  been  given 
in  Annex  A. 

The  details  given  in  Tables  2  to  7  are  for  information  only. 

In  the  preparation  of  this  standaid,  assistance  has  been  derived  from  the  following: 

BS  638  :  1966  Specification  for  arc  welding  plant,  equipment  and  accessories.   British  Standards 
Institution  (  UK  ). 

IEC  Pub  245-6    Rubber   insulated  cables  of  lated  voltage  up  to  and  including  450/750  volts 
(  arc  welding  electrode  cables).      International  Electrotechnical  Commission  (  IEC). 

For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  paiticular  requirement  of  this  standard  is  complied  with, 
the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  expressing  the  result  of  a  test  or  analysis,  shall  be  rounded 
off  in  accordance  with  IS  2  :  1960  'Rules  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  (revised)* .  The 
number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  oil  value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the 
specified  value  in  this  standard.

Indian  Standard 

WELDING  CABLES  — SPECIFICATION 

(  First  Revision  ) 


SECTION  1     GENERAL 

1  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  covers  the  requirements  and 
tests  for  single  core  flexible  cables  used  m 
welding  circuits. 

1*2  The  cables  covered  in  this  standard  arc 
suitable  for  use  where  combination  of  ambient 
temperature  and  the  temperature  due  to  load 
results  in  a  steady  conductor  temperature  not 
exceeding: 

a)  60°C  for  general  service  normal  duty 
elastomeric  compound;  and 

b)  90°C  for  heat  resisting  oil  resisting  flame 
retardant  (  HOFR  )  normal  duty  elasto- 
meric compound. 

The  selection  of  the  type  of  compound  rests 
with  the  purchaser. 

2  REFERENCES 

2.1  The  following  Indian  standards  ate  neces- 
sary adjuncts  to  this  standard: 


IS  No. 

1885 

(Part  32):  1971 


4905  :  1968 
6380  :  1984 

8130  :  1984 


10810 

(Part  44):  1984

and  accessories  for  electricity

Methods  of  test  for  cables*

3  TERMINOLOGY 

3.1  For  the  purpose  of  this  standard,  the  follow- 
ing definitions  in  addition  to  those  given  in 
IS  1885  (  Part  32  )  :  1971  shall  apply 

3.2  Acceptance  Test 

Tests  carried  out  on  samples  taken  from  a  lot 
for  the  purpose  of  acceptance  of  the  lot. 


3.3  Routine  Tests 

Tests  made  by  the  manufacturer  on  all  finished 
cable  lengths  to  demonstrate  the  integrity  of  the 
cable. 

3.4  Type  Tests 

Tests  required  to  be  made  before  supply  on  a 
geneial  commercial  basis  on  a  type  of  cable  in 
order  to  demonstrate  satisfactory  performance 
characteristics  to  meet  the  intended  application. 

NOlt  —  'I  hese  tests  arc  of  such  a  nature  that  after  they 
have  been  made,  they  need  not  be  repeated  unless 
changes  are  made  in  the  cable  materials  design,  which 
might  change  the  performance  characteristics 

SECTION  2     MATERIALS 
4  CONDUCTOR 

4.1  Copper  Conductor 

The  conductor  shall  be  composed  of  plain  or 
tinned  annealed  high  conductivity  copper  wires 
complying  with  IS  8130  :  1984. 

4.2  Aluminium  Conductor 

The  conductor  shall  be  composed  of  aluminium 
wires  complying  with  IS  8130  *  1984 

5  SEPARATOR 

5.1  The  maleiial  shall  be  dry  paper,  polyester 
tape  or  any  other  suitable  material 

6  COVERING 

6.1  The  general  service  normal  duty  elastomeric 
compound  shall  be  Type  SE1  conforming  to  the 
requirements  of  IS  6380  :  1984. 

6.2  The  heat  resisting,  oil  resisting  and  flame 
letardant  (HOFR)  noimal  duty  elastomeric 
compound  shall  be  Type  SE  3  conforming  to  the 
requirements  of  IS  6380  •  1984 

SECTION  3     CONSTRUCTION 

7  CONDUCTOR 

7.1  Circular  Copper  Conductor 

The  conductor  formation  shall  be  according  to 
Table  4  of  IS  8130  :  1984. 


IS  9S57  s  1990 


7.2  Circular  Aluminium  Conductor 

The  conductor  formation  shall  be  according  to 
Table  5  of  IS  8130:  1984. 

8  SEPARATOR 

8.1  The  conductor  shall  be  covered  with  a 
separator  (see  5.1 ).  The  separator  tape  shall  be 
so  applied  as  to  give  complete  coverage  of  the 
conductor. 

9  COVERING 

9.1  The  covering  shall  consist  of  one  of  the 
following  applied  over  the  conductor  and  the 
separator: 

a)  A  layer  of  general  service  normal  duty 
elastomeric  compound  in  accordance 
with  6.1,  or 

b)  A  layer  of  heat  resisting  oil  resisting  flame 
retardant  (  HOFR  )  normal  duty  elasto- 
mer ic  compound  in  accordance  with  6.2. 

9.2  Thickness  of  Covering 

The  average  thickness  of  the  covering  shall  be 
not  less  than  the  nominal  value  ( tc  )  specified  in 
Table  1. 

Table  1     Thickness  of  Covering

NOTE  —  Where  greater  flexibility  is  required,  it  may 
be  obtained  by  using  two  small  cables  in  parallel 
instead  of  one  equivalent  larger  cable. 


9.3  Tolerance  on  Thickness  of  Covering 

The  smallest  of  the  measured  values  of  the 
thickness  of  covering  shall  not  fall  below  the 
nominal  value  (  /c  in  mm  )  specified  in  Table  1 
by  more  than  010  mm  -f  0*15  tc. 

9.4  Application  of  Covering 

The  covering  shall  be  so  applied  that  it  fits 
closely  on  the  taped  conductor.  The  covering, 


unless   applied   by  extrusion   method,  shall  be 
applied  in  two  or  more  layers. 

9.5  The  colour  of  the  covering  shall  be  black.

10.2  Acceptance  Tests 

The   following  shall  constitute  acceptance  tests 
(  requirements  and  tests  methods  as  in  10.1  ): 

a)  Annealing  test, 

b)  Conductor  resistance  test, 

c)  Test  for  thickness  of  covering,  and 

d)  High  voltage  test  (  water  immersion  test ). 


IS  9857  '  1990 


10*2.1  A  recommended  sampling  plan  for 
acceptance  tests  is  given  in  Annex  B. 

10.3  Routine  Tests 

The  following  shall  constitute  routine  tests: 

a)  Conductor  resistance  test  (requirement 
and  test  method  as  in  10,1 ),  and 

b)  High  voltage  test  (water  immersion  test  ) 
(  requirement  and  test  method  as  in  11.1  ) 
or  spark  test   (  11.2  ). 

11  DETAILS  OF  TESTS 

11.1  High  Voltage  Test  (  Water  Immersion 

Test) 

The  voltage  shall  be  applied  after  the  cable  has 
been  immersed  in  water  for  not  less  than  12 
hours.  The  test  voltage  shall  be  applied  between 
the  water  in  which  the  cable  is  immersed  which 
shall  be  earthed,  and  the  conductor.  The  test 
shall  be  made  at  room  temperature  with  an  ac 
voltage  of  1  000  V  (rms)  at  a  frequency  of  40 
to  60  Hz.  The  voltage  shall  be  increased 
gradually  and  maintained  at  the  full  value  for 
5  minutes  without  breakdown. 

11.2  Spark  Test 

As  a  routine  test,  the  spark  test  in  accordance 
with  IS  10810  (Part  44)  :  1984  may  be  applied 
as  an  alternative  to  high  voltage  test  of  11.1 
to  cables  having  a  nominal  area  of  conductor 
50  mm2  and  below  and  the  spark  test  voltage 
shall  be  3  5  kV  ac. 


only      applicable 
Type  SE3. 


to    cable    with    covering    of

deration. 

11.4  Flammability  Test 

Period  of  burning  after  removal  of  the  flame 
shall  not  exceed  60  seconds  and  the  unaffected 
(  uncharred  )  portion  from  the  lower  edge  of  the 
top  clamp  shall  be  at  least  50  mm.  This  test  is

SECTION  5     IDENTIFICATION, 
PACKING  AND  MARKING 

12  IDENTIFICATION 

12.1  Manufacturer's  Identification 

The  manufacturer  shall  be  identified  throughout 
the  length  of  the  cable  by  means  of  a  tape 
bearing  the  indication  of  the  source  of  manu- 
facture being  printed,  indented  or  embossed 
on  the  cable.  In  case  none  of  these  methods 
can  be  applied  or  if  the  purchaser  so  desires, 
colour  identification  threads  in  accordance  with 
a  scheme  to  be  approved  by  the  Bureau  of 
Indian  Standards  shall  be  employed.  The 
distance  between  any  two  consecutive  printings, 
indentations  or  embossings  shall  be  not  more 
than  1  m. 

12.2  Cable  Identification 

Gables  with  HOFR  compound  shall  be  identified 
throughout  the  length  by  legend  *HR  90*  on  a 
tape  placed  inside  the  cable  or  by  printing, 
indenting  or  embossing  on  the  cable. 

12.3  Cable  Code 

The  following  code  shall  be  used  for  designating 
the  cable: 


Constituent 
Aluminium 
Elastomeric  covering 


Code  Letter 
A 
R 


NOTE  —  No     code     letter      is      required      for      copper 
conductor. 

13  PACKING  AND  MARKING 

13.1  The  cable  shall  be  either  wound  on  reels  or 
drums  or  supplied  in  coils  packed  and  labelled. 

13.2  The  label  or  the  stencilling  on  the   drum 
shall  contain  the  following  information: 

a)  Reference  to  this  Indian  Standard; 

b)  Indication  of  the  source  of  manufacture; 

c)  Type  of  cable; 

d)  Nominal      cross-sectional      area      of     the 
conductor; 

e)  Gable  code; 

f)  Length  of  cable  on  the  drum,  reel  or  coil; 

g)  Number  of  lengths  on  the  drum,  reel  or 
coil  (  if  more  than  one  ); 


If  M57  1 1990 


h)   Direction    of  rotation   of  the    drum  ( by 
means  of  an  arrow  ); 

j)  Approximate  gross  weight; 

k)  Country  of  manufacture;  and 

m)  Year  of  manufacture. 

14  GABLE  RATINGS 

14.1  The  maximum  current  ratings  of  flexible 
welding  cables  based  on  an  ambient  air  tem- 
perature of  30*C  are  given  in  Tables  2  and  4  for 
a  maximum  conductor  temperature  of  60°C  and 
in  Tables  3  and  5  for  maximum  conductor 
temperature  of  90°C.  The  percentage  duty 
cycles  given  in  Tables  2,  3,  4  and  5  are  based 
on  a  cycle  time  of  5  minutes. 

14JE  The  current  ratings  for  duty  cycles  other 
than  those  given  in  Tables  2,  3,  4  and  5  can  be 
calculated  using  the  following  formula: 


/i-MlOO/f)1 


where 


/c  —  current    rating    at     100    percent 
duty  cycle,  and 

F  —  required  duty  factor  expressed  as 
a  percentage. 

14.2.1  The  following  are  typical  duty  cycles  for 
various  welding  processes  and  applications: 


Up  to  100  percent 
30  to  85  percent 

30  to  60  percent 
Up  to  20  percent 


II  ■■  current    rating    at    the   required 
duty  cycles, 


a)  Automatic  welding 

b)  Semi-automatic 
welding 

c)  Manual  welding 

d)  Very  intermittent 
or  occasional  weld- 
ing 

15  VOLTAGE  DROP 


15.1  When  total  cable  lengths  in  excess  of  15  m 
are  involved,  it  may  be  necessary  to  use  cables 
of  larger  cross-section  to  ensure  that  the  voltage 
drop  is  not  exceysive  and  welding  currents  are 
maintained  at  adequate  levels.  Tables  6  and  J 
showing  the  dc  voltage  drop  at  normal  and 
elevated  temperatures  are  given  for  guidance.

ANNEX  A 
(  Ref.  Foreword ) 
LIMITATIONS  OF  ALUMINIUM  GABLES 


The  following  are  the  limitations  of  aluminium 
cables  compared  with  copper: 

a)  Terminations  have  to  be  suitable  for  use 
with  aluminium  cable, 

b)  There    is    a    reduced    service    life    whore 


flexibility  is  involved, 

c)  The  conductors  are  subject  to  atmospheric 
corrosion,  and 

d)  The  cable  size  is  large  for  similar  electrical 
properties  which  may  cause  difficulties  in 
matching  with  other  items  of  equipment. 


ANNEX     B 

(Clause  10,2.1  ) 

SAMPLING  OF  GABLES 


B-l  LOT 


B-l.l  In  any  consignment,  cables  of  the  same 
size  and  type  manufactured  under  essentially 
similar  conditions  of  production  shall  be  grouped 
together  to  constitute  a  lot. 

B-2  SCALE  OF  SAMPLING 

B-2.1  Samples  shall  be  taken  and  tested  from 
each  lot  for  ascertaining  the  conformity  of  the 
lot  to  the  requirements  of  the  specification. 

B-2.2  The  number  of  samples  to,  be  selected  shall 
depend  on  col  1  and  2  of  Table  8.  These 
samples  shall  be  taken  at  random. 

B-2.2. 1  In  order  to  ensure  the  randomness  of 
selection,  the  procedure  given  in  IS  4905  :  1968 
may  be  followed. 

B-3  NUMBER  OF  TESTS  AND  CRITERION 
FOR  CONFORMITY 

B-3.1  From  each  of  the  drums  selected  accord- 
ing to  col  1  and  2    of  Table  8,  suitable  lengths 


of  test  samples  shall  be  taken.  These  test  samples 
shall  be  subjected  to  each  of  the  acceptance  tests 
(  see  10.2  ).  A  test  sample  is  called  defective  if  it 
fails  in  any  one  of  the  acceptance  tests.  If  the 
number  of  defectives  is  less  than  or  equal  to  the 
corresponding  permissible  number  given  in  col  3, 
the  lot  shall  be  declared  as  conforming  to  the 
requirements  of  acceptance  tests,  otherwise 
not.

(Clauses  8.2.2  and  8.3.1  )

Bureau  of  Indian  Standards 

BIS  is  a  statutory  institution  established  under  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  Actr  1986  to  promote 
harmonious  development  of  the  activities  of  standardization,  marking  and  quality  certification  of  goods  and 
attending  to  connected  matters  in  the  country. 

Copyright 

BIS  has  the  copyright  ol  all  its  publications.  No  part  of  these  publications  may  be  reproduced  in  any  form 
without  the  prior  permission  in  writing  of  BIS.  This  docs  not  preclude  the  free  use,  in  the  course  of 
implementing  the  standard,  of  necessary  details,  such  as  symbols  and  sizes,  type  or  grade  designations. 
Enquiries  relating  to  copyright  be  addressed  to  the  Director  (Publication),  BIS. 

Review  of  Indian  Standards 

Amendments  are  issued  to  standards  as  the  need  arises  on  the  basis  of  comments.  Standards  are  also  reviewed 
periodically;  a  standard  along  with  amendments  is  reaffirmed  when  such  review  indicates  that  no  changes  are 
needed;  if  the  review  indicates  that  changes  are  needed,  it  is  taken  up  for  revision.  Users  of  Indian  Standards 
should  ascertain  that  they  are  in  possession  of  the  latest  amendments  or  edition  by  referring  to  the  latest  issue 
ol  'BIS  Handbook*  and  'Standards  Monthly  Additions'.
